title: Nine States Had Rejected DOJ Voter-Data Lawsuits by June 2026
description_short: AP reported that courts in nine states had rejected DOJ lawsuits seeking detailed voter-registration data, including Maryland.
description_medium: On June 23, 2026, the Associated Press reported that U.S. District Judge Stephanie Gallagher dismissed the Justice Department’s suit seeking Maryland’s detailed voter records. Gallagher wrote that the state’s unredacted voter file was not a record it had to provide under federal civil-rights law. AP said similar court losses then stood at nine states and that the department had sued in 30 states and the District of Columbia.
description_long: The Associated Press reported on June 23, 2026, that U.S. District Judge Stephanie Gallagher dismissed the Justice Department’s suit seeking Maryland’s detailed voter-registration records. Gallagher, appointed by President Donald Trump during his first term, wrote that she “joins every court to have addressed this issue” in concluding that the unredacted voter file was not a record Maryland had to produce to the United States. The Justice Department relied on an opinion from its Office of Legal Counsel asserting a right to the data under federal civil-rights law; Gallagher wrote that the court would not interpret the Civil Rights Act contrary to its text simply because the office advancing that view had adopted it. AP said the records sought included dates of birth, addresses, driver’s-license numbers and partial Social Security numbers. It reported that Maryland brought the number of states where courts had rejected similar demands to nine, and that DOJ had sued in 30 states and the District of Columbia. The AP report also identified similar rulings in Arizona, California, Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, Oregon, Rhode Island and Wisconsin. It described a Georgia dismissal as based on filing in the wrong city, after which DOJ refiled elsewhere.

source_fact_map.quote: U.S. District Court Judge Stephanie Gallagher last week dismissed a Justice Department lawsuit against Maryland that sought access to the state’s voter records.

Gallagher, appointed by Republican President Donald Trump during his first term, wrote that she “joins every court to have addressed this issue” in concluding that the unredacted voter registration file “is not a record or paper that a state must produce to the United States.”

The department has sued to force release of detailed state voter data — which includes dates of birth, addresses, driver’s license numbers and partial Social Security numbers — in 30 states and the District of Columbia.

In the Maryland case, the Justice Department tried to cite an opinion written by its own legal counsel’s office that it had the right to the state voter records under federal civil rights law, but Gallagher was not persuaded.
“The Court will not interpret the (Civil Rights Act) contrary to its text simply because an office of the party advancing that interpretation has adopted it,” she wrote.
With the dismissal Thursday in Maryland, the number of states where the Justice Department has lost similar cases comes to nine.
In addition to Maryland, judges have rejected those attempts in Arizona, California, Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, Oregon, Rhode Island and Wisconsin.
In Georgia, a judge dismissed a Justice Department lawsuit because it had been filed in the wrong city, prompting the government to refile elsewhere.
